_why: Inputs for the ReDoS benchmarks, shared by tools/run_tests.sh (Python) and
web/tools/parity.mjs (V8) so both engines are measured against the same shapes.
THE PRINCIPLE, and the previous version got it backwards. A seed must carry the
literal a rule requires, or the engine's required-character scan skips the input
and the timing measures the skip. But it must then WITHHOLD THE TAIL, because
catastrophic backtracking lives on the FAILING path: an input that matches
returns early and measures nothing.
Seeds built from pattern HEADS alone measured the matching path. Removing the
lookbehind from CREDENTIAL_ASSIGN, the documented quadratic, took 0.3ms against a
head-based seed and 8,491ms against a tail-withheld one at 16KB, and 134,969ms at
64KB. The benchmark would have passed a 135-second regression.
Each entry is a motif repeated to fill the size. Every motif contains the rule's
required literal and is constructed so no attempt can ever complete.
SEED PER BACKTRACKING SITE, NOT PER RULE. A rule can have more than one. The
database rule has two: the scheme scan and the credential-part scan. Withholding
the @ exercises the second; the quadratic that actually shipped lived in the
first, and no seed here contained a long dotted run, so removing the {0,31}
scheme bound measured 0.2ms and passed. Seeds are named for the site they
reach.
THE THREE PASSWORD SEEDS ADDED 2026-09-02, and why the two that were here
already could not fire. `password:        ` and `password= a a a a a ` both
contain WHITESPACE, which caps every value-side lookahead at the next space
and makes each one O(1). The quadratic needs a trigger word, a value, and no
whitespace anywhere, so the run never ends and each lookahead scans to the
end of the body at every candidate start. With the shipped seeds this gate
reported PASS, worst ratio x2.0, worst 1.4 ms, while the real cost at the
endpoint's own 256 KB cap was 42 seconds. Adding `PASS=x.` alone turns it to
FAIL at x4.0. The instrument was sound; it had never been given the shape.
ALL THREE FIRE INDIVIDUALLY. Measured with the bound reverted and one seed
present at a time, each on its own turns this gate red:
password-weak-trigger-no-whitespace   FAIL, ratio 4.0
password-weak-trigger-underscore      FAIL, ratio 3.9
password-strong-trigger-dotted        FAIL, ratio 3.9
Per-seed ratios over five repeats each, on the instrument the gate uses:
3.96-4.09, 3.94-4.02 and 3.79-3.94. Not one flip in fifteen measurements, and
the threshold is 3.0. The two pre-existing password seeds sit at a flat 2.0,
because they contain whitespace and every value lookahead is therefore O(1).
AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE SAID ONLY THE FIRST SEED WAS LOAD-BEARING AND
THE OTHER TWO WERE COVER. That was wrong and would have got two working seeds
deleted by somebody tidying up. It came from running the full set twice and
reading the ONE NAME the gate prints, which is `seedWorstRatio`, the maximum.
The first two seeds are within 5% of each other, so the winner's name changes
between runs. A seed that never wins has not failed to fire; it is simply not
the loudest. Read the per-seed ratio, never the reported maximum, before
concluding anything about which seed does the work.
The weak trigger (`PASS`, `_pass`) is the expensive one and is listed first:

seeds.password-assign-spaces: password= a a a a a
